missions.title: A Bridge in Two Views
missions.knowledgeQuestion: How can two different pictures of one thing both be faithful?

objectives.title: Fit the tracings to the two views of the bridge.

missions.title: The Creek Keeps Its Own Time
missions.knowledgeQuestion: How far can marks from one storm guide the next decision?
missions.stake: Ayla needs to return the dawn watch notes dry. A short rail helps the watch crew, and the sheltered bend has room for a cart.

objectives.title: Check the high-water marks and the cart track.
Choose a storm path with Ayla at the clearing.
Carry the watch notes through the route you opened.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: On this level strip of bank you’re looking straight along the bridge rail. The end post hides the lower post. The joiner set a frame on this exact spot. A blank tracing strip fits in its groove.

options.text: Slide in a strip. Mark the post you can see.
Leave the frame in place.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: You draw one dark edge. The frame has a WEST notch and a flat base. You copy those marks onto the corner of the strip. The joiner’s bench in the clearing has a space for this view.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: From this rise you see across the rail instead of along it. There are two posts with a little daylight between them. This frame stands above the bridge deck, tilted to match that view.

options.text: Trace both posts and mark the space between them.
Leave the frame in place.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: You run the pencil along both edges. The EAST notch and the rise mark go on the corner. At the joiner’s bench, this view can go beside the one from the bank.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: The joiner is building a guide to the old rail. People stop here to sketch the bridge, and some go straight to a crossing. A note asks for two drawings: one through the west-bank frame and one through the frame on the east rise. The bench has room for one hinged guide or for two small approach panels.

options.text: Mount the two tracings back to back on the hinged guide.
Set each tracing in its own panel and hang it at its approach.
Look for the frames first.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: You set the west tracing against one face of the guide and the taller east view against the other. Each leaf gets a label you can read below the picture. Try turning it at the bench, where a visitor can compare both pictures in one place.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: You give the joiner a panel for each bank, with a small arrow for where to stand. People can walk up to the rail with the view in hand. Check each panel on the trail. The joiner leaves the two outlines on this bench.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: The cutouts on the bench show which panels went out. The west panel hangs by the level bank. The east panel is on the rise. The two pictures still share the same scale mark.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: The guide swings on one hinge. A thin raised line along each lower edge shows the bridge deck. The leaves read LEVEL BANK and RISE.

options.text: Turn the leaf marked LEVEL BANK.
Turn the leaf marked RISE.
Step back from the guide.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: From the level bank, the end post covers the lower post. The joiner has put a blank space where your view stops. Both leaves have a scale mark for one plank, so readers can check how far the tracing runs.

options.text: Turn the leaf marked RISE.
Leave the guide standing.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: The RISE leaf shows two posts. A visitor turns it at the hinge and asks which standing place would bring those lines together. The guide puts the two places beside the drawings.

options.text: Turn the leaf marked LEVEL BANK.
Leave the guide standing.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: The west-bank panel hangs beside the old rail. One post sits in front of the other from here. Move to the notch on the bank and line up the drawing’s raised deck line with the actual deck.

options.text: Line up the deck with the west notch.
Walk on.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: The drawn edges meet the real edges. A walker traces the line and adds WEST BANK to the sketch that will go home. The small arrow on the panel points to the other view.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: At the rise the two posts separate. The east panel has the same deck line as the west panel. There is room to put a finger between the drawn posts.

options.text: Line up the deck with the east notch.
Walk on.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: From the rise, the gap in the tracing sits over the gap in the rail. A walker points to the lower post, then turns to see what hides it from the bank. The panel keeps both viewing places on its edge.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: Water rattles the stones below the north landing. Two wet lines cross the post. The crew scratched the morning bell beside the higher one and the noon bell beside the lower one. Move the loose date slip into the groove and see which mark it fits.

options.text: Fit the two dates alongside the marks.
Leave the post and dates where they are.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: The water here fell between the bells and stayed below the north landing at noon. There is room to unfold the rail for one keeper. The post says what happened at this spot. The bend isn’t in view.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: A strip of fresh cart tracks curls around the alder. The paper on a dry trunk gives the cart crew’s noon check. Its wheel marks stop by the spare wind screen. Follow the track on the field sketch and match it to the paper.

options.text: Lay the cart crew’s paper over this part of the sketch.
Leave the sketch at the alder.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: The cart crew found its bend dry after the morning rise. There is room for a cart between the screen posts. The wind rattles the empty case where the dawn notes should sit. The creek marks upstream don’t show this bend.

dialogue.speaker: forest-steward
dialogue.text: The edge of my dawn notebook is curling. My sister can take the usual round for the dry case, or we can open one of the spare storm paths. The north rail is short and narrow. The bend is longer and takes a cart. Bring me the post dates and the cart crew’s paper.

options.text: Unfold the north rail for the note carriers.
Fit the wind screen at the bend so carts can use it.
One gauge on the Observatory Coast could only speak for its own site.
Let the creek keep its own time. Take the usual round.
Read which route we left open.
Keep the board ready.

dialogue.speaker: forest-steward
dialogue.text: Then we have the same job here. The post puts two times on one spot. The cart crew gives us another place. Keep both papers with the route we open.

options.text: Unfold the north rail for the note carriers.
Fit the wind screen at the bend so carts can use it.
Let the creek keep its own time. Take the usual round.

dialogue.speaker: forest-steward
dialogue.text: I’ll unfold the north keeper’s rail. The note case can cross close to the lookout. A cart will still need the ordinary bridge. Take the rail now if you like. The creek can rattle all it wants below us.

dialogue.speaker: forest-steward
dialogue.text: I’ll fit the reed wind screen at the bend. The cart can take the dry note case and the next crew’s lanterns together. We’ll go the long way. I’ve saved the crew one song for that part.

dialogue.speaker: forest-steward
dialogue.text: The creek has missed its appointment anyway. I’ll send my sister round the usual bridge. The fittings stay here if another watch wants them. Your papers can wait at this board.

dialogue.speaker: forest-steward
dialogue.text: Both readings stay here with the chosen route strip. Leave today’s times on them. My sister will need her own checks next time the creek moves.

hints.text: A view changes when the observer changes banks.
Look for the sketch frames on the level west bank and the east rise.
Put the two tracings on the joiner’s bench in the clearing. Decide where readers should meet them.
Turn both leaves at the bench, or follow the trail and line up the two approach panels.
Ayla has two things to compare before opening a storm path.
The wet post stands north of the west-bank frame. The cart track ends at the south-east alder bend.
Line up both dates at the wet post. Match the cart crew’s paper against the sketch at the bend.
Check the two wet lines on the west bank of Listening Trail and the cart track on the east side. The ordinary bridge and ford connect the banks.
Ayla keeps the spare route fittings beside her storm board.
Take both reports to the board in Bridge Clearing.
A smaller group can use the short rail. A cart fits the longer bend.
Use Ayla’s storm-route board. Choose the rail or the bend. The usual round stays available if you want to leave it.
The two sides of the chosen crossing show the same new aid.
The keeper’s rail is in the north. The cart crossing and its screen are at the south bend.
Approach the aid on either bank and use the crossing.
On Listening Trail use the opened rail or the screened crossing. The return slip will be at Fern Station.

journal.text: The two bridge tracings became a guide. They keep each standing place with its drawing. From the west the end post covers the lower one. From the rise both posts are in view.

The creek marks put two readings in one place. The cart crew’s tracks added a view of the bend. The route we opened carried the notes. The crew kept the two places and their times with the next watch’s copy.
